title: Tighten lb: rigorous primal Rayleigh lower bound for trace-constrained max-eigenvalue blocks
description: The single-dual Jansson lower bound (b18/b19) is structurally loose for max-eigenvalue problems: lb = b^T y_ext + min(0,lambda_min(Z_ext))*xbar is stuck at lambda_min(C) regardless of y_ext (e.g. [1,3] for max_eigenvalue_2x2, opt=3=lambda_max(C)). The flagship use case (max eigenvalue / ground-state-energy lower bounds, PRD 1.2) thus gets a vacuous lower bound. FIX: a rigorous PRIMAL lower bound = <C,Xhat> for a rigorously-feasible Xhat. For a single trace constraint <I,X>=b_1 (X PSD), Xhat = b_1 * v v^T/(v^T v) is exactly trace-b_1 and exactly PSD (rank-1, no projection/Cholesky), so lb = b_1*(v^T C v)/(v^T v) <= b_1*lambda_max(C) = opt for ANY v (Rayleigh <= lambda_max), tight when v ~ top eigenvector (from the solver X~). Integrate as lb = max(dual-residual lb, primal Rayleigh lb) in certify_bracket. SCOPE: single-block single-trace-constraint (A_1=I): max_eigenvalue_2x2, max_eig_tridiag_3x3, max_eig_path_4/8/16. Per-block-trace (separable_12block) + general higher-rank/multi-constraint primal projection (two_block_corr_coupled; relates to 9tm) are follow-ups. TDD + mutation check + bracket-contains-optimum rigor gate.
close_reason: Tight rigorous primal lower bound shipped for single-block single-trace max-eigenvalue problems. The dual-residual lb is structurally stuck at lambda_min(C) (e.g. [1,3] for max_eigenvalue_2x2, opt=3). Fix: arbsdp_primal_lower_bound -- a feasible rank-1 point X_hat=b1*v v^T/(v^T v) gives lb=b1*(v^T C v)/(v^T v) <= opt for ANY v (Rayleigh<=lambda_max; PSD by construction, no Cholesky; rigorous in ball arithmetic). certify_bracket returns lb=max(dual,primal). Measured: max_eigenvalue_2x2/tridiag_3x3/path_4 lb moves from lambda_min(C) (gap~2) to within ~2^-192 of opt; independently verified lb<=true closed-form opt (3, 2+sqrt3, (5+sqrt5)/2) at 640 bits, 0 violations. FINDING: 65-digit golden refs are only enclosures of irrational optima; tests now compare against a true-opt enclosure + closed-form oracle (rule 2: widen the reference, not the bound). 14/14 ctest normal+ASan, zero leaks. Mutation-checked: disable primal -> tightness fails; inflate lb -> rigor gate fails. Follow-up (per-block + general higher-rank/coupled): arb-prec-IPM-oc7.

title: Verify Jansson lb a-priori-bound convention (trace vs Loewner / block-dim factor) before b18/b19
description: b27 audition flagged that JCK 2007 Thm 3.2 / Lemma 3.1 carry a block-dimension factor s_b: lb = b^T y + sum_b s_b*min(0,d_b)*xbar_b. VERIFIED (independent derivation): that factor arises ONLY under a Loewner/eigenvalue a-priori bound (X <= xbar*I => tr X <= s_b*xbar). Our MATH_SPEC 5.4 uses a TRACE bound (xbar >= tr X); under the trace convention tr(DX) >= lambda_min(D)*tr(X) >= min(0,lambda_min(D))*xbar with NO s_b factor (for lambda_min<0, tr(X)<=xbar flips the product). So 5.4 is CORRECT as written for the trace convention; the audition mis-mapped JCK's Loewner convention onto ours. ACTION (b18/b19, NOT b17): (1) the a-priori-bound API must document + enforce xbar_b = TRACE bound (a Loewner/lambda_max bound supplied without *s_b would over-state lb -> P0 exclusion of the optimum, rule 2); (2) every golden's xbar_b must be a trace bound; (3) add a bracket-contains-optimum property test for a MULTI-ELEMENT block (n_b>=2) with a NEGATIVE d_b -- the exact case a convention slip would expose (LP/1x1 blocks have s_b=1 and hide it). Reconfirm against JCK 2007 directly when writing the b18 assembly + the b19 ub/ybar derivation.
close_reason: Trace-bound convention verified (no JCK s_b factor) + guarded by a discriminating test. (1) Re-verified vs JCK 2007 (SIAM J. Numer. Anal. 46(1):180-200): s_b is Loewner-only (Lemma 3.1 sums s_b eigenvector terms); our trace form tr(DX)>=min(0,lambda_min(D))*xbar has no factor. CLAUDE.md citation corrected. (2) Audited all 7 rigor-gate goldens: each xbar is an EXACT trace bound (trace pinned by diagonal equality constraints; max-eig tr=1, two_block_corr_coupled tr=3/blk). (3) New test_trace_vs_loewner: full-rank X*=I (n_b=2, tr=2, lambda_max=1, opt=2); TRACE xbar=2 brackets opt exactly, LOEWNER xbar=1 EXCLUDES (lb=2+2^-10, ub=2-2^-10). Mutation (rule 9): spurious s_b fails 4/6 assertions while rank-1 goldens stay green. 14/14 ctest normal+ASan, zero leaks.

title: L0 true-midpoint arithmetic: untrusted ball radii NaN-corrupt midpoints (the bits/digit lever)
description: b30 DIAGNOSIS (concrete): the Layer-0 point-mode solve runs on arb (ball) values, but the ball RADII -- which CLAUDE rule 1 says are NOT trusted in L0 -- still propagate. Near convergence the Schur condition number ~1/mu (PRD invariant 3) degrades the radius ~30-60 bits per IPM step until lambda_min's BALL straddles zero, so arb_rsqrt/arb_inv return a NaN MIDPOINT -> iterate_is_valid fails -> NUMERICAL -> the controller escalates precision. b30 confirmed X,S stay strictly PD at the failure (lambda_min(X)=9.52, lambda_min(S)=1.06e-13 > 0 for trivial_2x2 at prec 256) and the cone kernels are accurate (psd_invsqrt residual ~1e-54) -- so this is NOT a cone-exit, step-length, or kernel bug. It is the DOMINANT driver of the ~19-158 bits/digit on boundary-optimum goldens and the reason trivial_2x2 needs 512 bits (not <=256) for 15 digits. LEVER: make the L0 spectral/iterate arithmetic operate on pure MIDPOINTS (clear radii before the risky eig/sqrt/invsqrt/Schur ops, or use arf / arb_get_mid) so untrusted radii cannot NaN-corrupt the midpoint -- which is what rule 1 ('midpoints, radii not trusted') actually requires. PRD section 11.3 open decision (arb-midpoint vs arf for L0). AUDITION arf vs radius-clearing; measure bits/digit on the test_golden gate before/after.
acceptance_criteria: trivial_2x2 reaches 15 digits at materially lower final_prec than today's 512 (target the b30 goal of <=256); low-prec NUMs where X,S are genuinely PD become OPT; test_golden efficiency XFAILs move toward PASS (bits/digit down markedly); no correctness regression; TDD with measured before/after.
close_reason: L0 true-midpoint via RADIUS-CLEARING: iterate_clear_radii() in c/src/solve.c zeros untrusted iterate radii (X,S,y,tau,kappa) each IPM step (mag_zero(arb_radref), no alloc). arf rejected (FLINT 3.0.1 has no arf_mat: cho/eig/solve absent). Measured bits/digit: sdp_sqrt2 158->18, mixed_blocks 153->20, disparate_scale_sqrt2 153->38, max_eig_path_16 138->32, two_block_corr_coupled 131->33, trivial_2x2 15 digits at prec=256 (was 512). test_golden 16/16 corr=PASS eff=PASS (was 16 eff=XFAIL); suite 22.85s->6.37s; 12/12 ctest normal+ASan, zero leaks; objectives unchanged (no correctness regression). Residual efficiency (Schur cond + controller granularity) -> bead wdz. Acceptance MET (trivial 15 digits <=256 bits).

title: test_golden gate: trivial_2x2 & ill_conditioned_3x3 corr=FAIL at calibrated target_digits=12 (mu-gate vs objective-accuracy mismatch)
description:
FINDING from the new GATED golden-master runner c/test/test_golden.c (bead arb-prec-IPM-epic.1). With the runner setting pp.target_digits = c.target_digits (=12) and pp.prec_max = c.prec_cap as the contract requires, two goldens FAIL the CORRECTNESS class:

  trivial_2x2:         adaptive OPTIMAL, final_prec=128, iters=4, ONLY 6.7 / 12 objective digits.
  ill_conditioned_3x3: adaptive OPTIMAL, final_prec=128, iters=4, ONLY 8.9 / 12 objective digits.

ROOT CAUSE (reproduced, concrete numbers): these are the only two goldens whose prec0=128 solve SUCCEEDS (ARBSDP_SOLVE_OPTIMAL) at the loose inner gate (mu ~ 1.4e-11 / 1.75e-11 when target_digits=12 sets feas/opt_tol = 1e-12). The adaptive driver therefore STOPS immediately (prec_history_len=1, final_prec=128, never escalates) and returns ADAPTIVE_OPTIMAL even though the recovered OBJECTIVE midpoint is only ~6.7 / ~8.9 correct digits. The per-step digits(mu) for that solve is itself 10.8 (< 12), yet the adaptive layer still stamped OPTIMAL -> the accuracy gate accepts a mu-based proxy that does NOT guarantee the requested objective digits. The other 5 goldens hit NUMERICAL at prec0/256 (the b30 PSD-boundary brittleness), are FORCED to escalate to 512-1024 bits, and incidentally clear 11-14 digits -> corr=PASS.

PROVENANCE MISMATCH: the schema-v2 known_gaps[efficiency] reasons cite 14.2 (trivial) / 14.1 (ill) achieved digits at final_prec 1024. Those numbers were measured at the DEFAULT target_digits=30 (which forces escalation to 1024). At the CALIBRATED target_digits=12 the driver does not escalate and the achieved digits collapse to 6.7 / 8.9. So either (a) the adaptive accuracy gate is wrong (ADAPTIVE_OPTIMAL should require the recovered objective to actually meet target_digits, not just the mu proxy), or (b) target_digits=12 is unreachable for these two at prec0 and the provenance needs a correctness known_gap. Per CLAUDE.md the FIX is (a) tighten the gate / b30 cone-safety so a non-escalated low-prec solve cannot claim more accuracy than it delivers -- NOT loosen the test. Related to / blocked-by arb-prec-IPM-b30 (same point-mode PSD-boundary root cause).

REPRO: ./c/build/test_golden  -> GATE: FAIL, corr=FAIL on trivial_2x2 & ill_conditioned_3x3. The runner, CMake wiring, and the other classes are correct; the gate is RED because the finding is real.
notes: b30 OUTCOME: the trivial_2x2 & ill_conditioned_3x3 false-optimals are RESOLVED -- the b30 strict-PD gate (fail-loud psd_invsqrt) + the V3 gamma=0.9999 step tipped the fragile prec=128 soft-optimal to honest NUMERICAL-then-escalate, so both now reach their target_digits (test_golden corr=PASS) and their stale correctness known_gaps were removed. No current golden reproduces the false-optimal. BUT the PRINCIPLED contract fix is still owed (this stays OPEN): the adaptive controller still accepts a 6-flag OPTIMAL at inner tol 10^-target as proof of target_digits without validating the recovered objective enclosure or setting a prec floor from target_digits (PRD 4.3); it could resurface on the epic.2/epic.3 punishing problems. Resolution was incidental to b30, not a principled controller fix.
close_reason: Fixed via cross-precision STABILITY gate (arbsdp_adaptive_confirmed in c/src/precision.c): an OPTIMAL fixed solve at precision P is only a CANDIDATE; the next doubling (2P) CONFIRMS it iff that solve is also OPTIMAL and its recovered objective agrees with the candidate to >= target_digits (relative). On confirmation the controller RETURNS THE CANDIDATE (final_prec stays at P; confirming solve is verification overhead) -> zero bits/digit regression, zero provenance change. Catches the p68 class (precision-starved OPTIMAL whose value moves when precision rises is rejected). Measurement (de-risk): post-b30 all 16 goldens already deliver digits>=target with favorable mu->objective transfer (+0.6..+3.9), so the bug was latent (b30-masked); the simple digits_from_mu gate was REJECTED (would over-reject 13/16). TDD: RED unit test test_confirm_gate (4 constructed cases; status-only stub fails the p68 discriminator), GREEN impl + arbsdp_result_swap move helper, integration test test_p68_victims_confirmed (trivial_2x2 13.756d / ill_conditioned_3x3 13.744d at td=12, both ADAPTIVE_OPTIMAL, final_prec=128, prec_history_len=2 proving confirmation). ctest 14/14 normal+ASan, -Wall -Wextra clean, valgrind definitely/indirectly-lost=0. Docs aligned (precision.h banner, precision.c, MATH_SPEC §6, PRD §4.3) with honest point-mode-heuristic framing. RESIDUAL rigorous-accuracy gate (tolerance-limited case) -> arb-prec-IPM-wf5 (blocked on oc7).

title: P0: keep point-mode iterate strictly inside the PSD cone (correctness)
description: ROOT BRITTLENESS: every golden problem returns NUM at low precision and only OPT at the final precision (bench/brittle_probe.c: trivial_2x2 needs 1024 bits for 15 digits ~ 70 bits/digit vs ~3.3 needed; sdp_sqrt2 ceilings ~32 digits even at 20000 bits). The point-mode iterate is driven onto/over the PSD boundary instead of converging, then NT scaling (needs PD) breaks -> NUM. AUDITION best-in-class IPM cone-safety (CLAUDE rule 3): fraction-to-boundary gamma in [0.9,0.99] (the current Mehrotra safeguard clips to 0.999999 - far too aggressive, no margin), central-path neighborhood control, what SDPA/SDPT3/SeDuMi do to stay interior at high precision. Also: psd_invsqrt floors eigenvalues silently (linalg.c) producing garbage near singularity - make NT scaling / cone ops FAIL LOUD when X or S leaves the cone (rule 5) instead of producing garbage that becomes a late NUM. GOAL: converge to target tolerance at ~3-6 bits/digit (not 50-70); trivial_2x2 to 15 digits should NOT need 1024 bits. TDD with the bits-per-digit metric.
design: AUDITION (rule 3): step cap 0.999999 (~gamma=1.0) is a float64-era choice ported verbatim from TS HsdeNtSdpSolver.ts:1170; it lands the iterate on the PSD boundary, breaking NT scaling. psd_invsqrt floors eigenvalues at 1e-300 (PsdCone.ts:155) -> silent garbage. DECISION: (1) fraction-to-boundary alpha=min(1, gamma*alpha_to_boundary) with gamma=0.9 (SDPA-GMP default param.sdpa gammaStar=0.9 -- the arbitrary-precision SDP reference). Losers: 0.999999/1.0 (the bug); SDPB --stepLengthReduction=0.7 (more iters than our tiny problems need); SDPT3 sqlpmain.m adaptive 0.9+0.09*min(ap,ad) (needs separate primal/dual steps, our HSDE takes a single combined step). (2) Fail-loud cone ops: psd_invsqrt detects non-strictly-PD input and propagates an honest NUMERICAL cone-exit instead of the 1e-300 floor (rule 5); precision controller escalates. (3) NO neighborhood control -- production SDP solvers (SDPA/SDPT3/SeDuMi) don't gate on N_inf/N_2 at runtime; fraction-to-boundary + Tikhonov suffices (rule 14). p68 (controller prec-floor/objective-accuracy) stays separate, blocked by b30. cond(W)=Theta(1/mu) is handled by the existing adaptive precision escalation, not by tightening gamma near convergence.
acceptance_criteria: trivial_2x2/max_eig reach 15 digits at <= ~256 bits (not 1024); per-precision trajectories show OPT (not NUM) once precision suffices; cone ops fail loud on exit; bench/brittle_probe bits-per-digit improves markedly; TDD + golden cross-checks still pass.
close_reason: Delivered the cone-safety fixes: (1) step rule = TS Mehrotra max(0.95a,2a-1) capped at gamma=0.9999, chosen by an EMPIRICAL sweep over the 7 goldens (literature gamma=0.9 was falsified; pure fraction-to-boundary regressed). trivial_2x2 1024->512 bits for ~14 digits; all 7 reach target. (2) fail-loud cone ops: strict-PD gate replaces the silent 1e-300 floor; honest NUMERICAL on degradation (rule 5). Resolved the p68 false-optimals on trivial/ill_cond. 12/12 ctests both configs, test_golden GATE PASS, ASan clean. DIAGNOSIS CORRECTED: brittleness is point-mode precision exhaustion (untrusted ball radius -> NaN midpoint, cond~1/mu), NOT cone-exit (X,S stay PD); the residual bits/digit floor is precision-fundamental in arb-ball L0 -> the '15 digits at <=256 bits' target moves to epic.6 (true-midpoint L0 arithmetic). Commit 1763bde.

title: P0 BUG: read_sdpa heap-corrupts on non-init'd problem struct
description: arbsdp_read_sdpa (io.c:273) calls arbsdp_problem_clear(p) at entry, which frees p->b/p->mats. If the caller did NOT arbsdp_problem_init(p) first, those are garbage pointers -> heap corruption -> SIGSEGV (gdb: _int_free_merge_chunk <- arbsdp_problem_clear io.c:63 <- read_sdpa io.c:273). MASKED under ASan, MISSED by tests (they init). Found via bench/brittle_probe.c (remove the init line to repro). FIX: make read_sdpa foolproof - init internally (memset/zero the struct) instead of clearing at entry, OR clearly require+document an uninit contract AND never deref uninitialized fields. AUDITION the safe-API options. RED-GREEN: add a CTest that passes a zeroed/garbage struct to read_sdpa and must not corrupt the heap (run under the NORMAL build, not just ASan).
acceptance_criteria: a CTest exercises read_sdpa on a non-pre-init'd struct without crashing/corruption under the NORMAL build; bench/brittle_probe.c without the init line no longer segfaults; existing tests still green; ASan+normal clean.
close_reason: read_sdpa now arbsdp_problem_init(p)s at entry instead of arbsdp_problem_clear(p), so it never derefs/frees a non-init'd struct's garbage pointers (io.c). Contract documented in problem.h (foolproof; re-read must clear() first). RED-GREEN regression test_read_uninitialized in test_io.c: fills a struct with non-heap sentinels -> SIGSEGV (exit 139) on the old reader, PASS after. 11/11 ctests green in BOTH normal and ASan configs; brittle_probe without the init line no longer segfaults (exit 0). LeakSanitizer clean.

title: oc7(c): optional k-dim Rayleigh-Ritz subspace primal lower bound (clustered/degenerate top eigenvalues)
description: Optional refinement of the primal Rayleigh lb (oc7 part a/b). For DEGENERATE or CLUSTERED top eigenvalues a single Rayleigh vector v is sub-optimal; a k-dim Rayleigh-Ritz subspace V (k top eigenvectors of X~) gives a tighter rigorous bound: opt_b >= beta_b * lambda_max(V^T C_b V) computed via the verified-Cholesky-shift lambda_max on the small k x k Gram-projected matrix (reuse arbsdp_lambda_max_upper_bound machinery). Feasible point X_hat_b = beta_b * (V W V^T) for the optimal k x k W>=0 with tr(W)=1 (the top Ritz projector). Lower priority: the single-vector bound (oc7a) is already tight to ~1e-113 on the non-degenerate goldens; this only helps clustered spectra. Add a degenerate-spectrum golden as the cross-check.

title: Gate ADAPTIVE_OPTIMAL on Layer-1 certified bracket width (rigorous accuracy) once lb is tight
description: FOLLOW-UP from arb-prec-IPM-p68. The p68 fix made the adaptive accuracy gate a CROSS-PRECISION STABILITY heuristic (arbsdp_adaptive_confirmed): a candidate OPTIMAL@P is accepted only if the 2P solve is OPTIMAL and its recovered objective agrees to >= target_digits. This catches precision-limited inaccuracy and cross-precision instability (the p68 class), but per CLAUDE.md rule 1 it is still a POINT-MODE heuristic, NOT a rigorous objective-accuracy guarantee. RESIDUAL UNDETECTED CASE: two solves that both converge to the same tolerance-limited point agree with each other yet are both short of the true optimum (adverse scaled-residual->objective transfer); the stability gate accepts them. The RIGOROUS fix is to gate ADAPTIVE_OPTIMAL (or add a rigorous-accuracy status) on the Layer-1 certified bracket width ub-lb <= 10^-target_digits (certify.c, b18/b19), which is derived independently in ball arithmetic. BLOCKED-BY: the bracket lb is currently loose off the single-block max-eig happy path (arb-prec-IPM-oc7); a bracket gate is premature until lb is tight for general problems. ACCEPTANCE: when oc7 lands, add a controller mode that escalates until the rigorous bracket meets target_digits, and document ADAPTIVE_OPTIMAL vs the new rigorous status. Measurement context: post-b30 all 16 goldens already deliver digits>=target with favorable mu->objective transfer (+0.6..+3.9 digits), so this is robustness for future punishing problems (epic.2/epic.3), not a current corpus failure.

title: UB-B: residual upper bound (ybar + primal PSD projection), Jansson 2009 Thm 4.2 fallback
description: The FINITE Layer-1 upper bound is UB-A (dual-side mirror of the lower bound, xbar-only, reusing arbsdp_lambda_min_lower_bound on -Z; implemented in b19). UB-B is the SECONDARY/fallback upper bound for when xbar is unavailable but a near-feasible primal Xtilde + a dual-norm bound ybar_i>=|y*_i| are: p*_ext <= <C_file,Xt+> + ybar^T r, where Xt+ is the block-wise PSD projection of Xtilde (shift each block by |min(0,lambda_min(X_b))|*I) and r_i >= |<A_i,Xt+>-b_i| is the rigorous primal residual (ball, upper endpoint). Needs primal-PSD-projection machinery not yet present. The arbsdp_apriori.ybar field + MATH_SPEC 5.5 'UB-B' + 10 decision 3 are reserved for this. Ref: Jansson 2009 Japan J Indust Appl Math 26:337-363 Thm 4.2; VSDP @vsdp/rigorous_upper_bound.m. Low priority: UB-A covers the in-scope tr-bounded goldens; UB-B matters for problems with a known dual bound but unbounded/unknown trace.
